summary.text: A 25-year-old woman presented to the outpatient clinic with a speech disorder and right-sided weakness. Examination showed slight effacement of the left nasolabial sulcus and hypoactive upper-extremity deep tendon reflexes. Cerebral MRI showed a 20 × 8 × 20 mm intradiploic cystic lesion in the left frontal skull region, hyperintense on T1- and T2-weighted images.

She underwent total resection of the lesion with mini-plate reconstruction, using neuronavigation, a curvilinear skin incision and high-speed drilling of the bony margins. Histopathology showed cavernous hemangioma. Her postoperative course was described as uneventful.

summary.text: A woman reported as 32 years old in the narrative (33 in Table 1) presented with chronic headache and right parietal swelling that grew from 2 cm to up to 4 cm after 2 months. She had a history of head trauma from a motor vehicle accident nearly 4.5 years earlier. Skull radiographs showed a wide radiolucent area with sclerotic margins at the right parietal region.

Cranial MRI showed a round CSF-filled cystic mass, hypointense on T1-weighted and hyperintense on T2-weighted images, with no contrast enhancement on post-contrast T1 images. Surgery involved a modified curvilinear incision, craniotomy with drainage of cystic contents, total resection and repair of the bony defect with porous polyethylene. Histopathology showed an arachnoid/leptomeningeal cyst and there were no complications.

article_limitations: Nine individual patients from the authors' series are annotated; Table 2 and the Discussion rows about published literature cases (Lloret, Colas, Garfinkle, Arana, Yim, Yalcin, Khodarahmi and unnamed rows) are cited cases, not patients of this article, and are not annotated as facts.

Cohort-level statements (median age, sex proportions, eight patients with headache, MRI available for eight patients, diagnosis confirmed by CT in one case, FLAIR hyperintensity in two epidermoid patients, expected treatment recommendations) are not copied to individuals unless a sentence names a diagnosis held by a single patient.
Table 1 columns Preoperative image and Postoperative image are Y/N availability flags, not clinical results, and are not recorded as observations.

Source conflicts kept review_only: Case 2 age 32 versus 33; Case 3 T1 signal hyperintense versus hypointense; Case 4 meningioma site left parietal versus left frontal and Fig. 4A modality T1 MR versus CT; Case 5 history of tuberous sclerosis versus absence of clinical findings; Case 6 laterality left versus right, diffusion isointense versus restricted, and total resection versus nonsurgical follow-up; Case 8 destroyed bone orbital versus parietal; Case 9 laterality right versus left and T1/FLAIR signal text versus caption/table.

Case 7 monitoring statement and the Results sentence about an arachnoid cyst patient with right parietal swelling cannot be mapped with certainty to Case 7 or Case 2; the monitoring item is review_only and no fact is created from the right parietal swelling sentence.
Case 2 narrative places findings of a preoperative type on a postoperative CT; kept as stated.
